newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van Leer set to sign new supply contract.
newsitem.headline: Van Leer set to sign new supply contract.

text.p: AMSTERDAM, March 24 (Reuter) Dutch industrial and consumer packaging group Van Leer NV is poised to sign a new global supply contract with a major chemicals multinational in the next six weeks or so, Van Leer chairman Bill de Vlugt said on Monday.
"You can expect a new (contract) in six weeks or so," he told a results news conference.
Van Leer is world market leader in steel drums for the petrochemicals industry with a 22 percent market share.
De Vlugt said Van Leer's global presence with industrial packaging operations in some 50 countries meant it was well-placed to win global supply contracts from multinationals.
Last year Van Leer signed such contracts with Dow Chemical, Bayer, Dupont and others, he said.
"It's a win-win situation which makes it possible to lower (selling) prices while maintaining margins," he said.
The world market for steel drums is virtually saturated, but Van Leer said it increased its market share last year.
"We now produce an added two million drums," De Vlugt said.
He declined to name the prospective client, but did say it was not Dutch chemicals group Akzo.
Van Leer earlier reported 1996 net profits available to ordinary shareholders up 22.4 percent at 96.9 million guilders.
In 1995 the company, which was launched on the Amsterdam bourse in May 1996, reported net profit available to ordinary shareholders of 79.2 million guilders.
